name: MBench-A environment recovery with uniform32 DA3 producer

da3.sampling: upstream sample_bgr_frames: numpy.linspace(0,total-1,min(32,total),dtype=int), cv2 seek/decode; require 32 distinct decoded samples
da3.pose_convention: invert actual world-to-camera as float32 4x4; retain camera-to-world [:,:3,:4]; original OpenCV reference world
da3.input_images: save original sampled BGR pixels; official geometry reader resizes to DA3 depth shape using cv2.INTER_LINEAR
da3.arrays: compact 32-frame depth/intrinsics/extrinsics; no interpolation or full-frame expansion
da3.pair_selector: unmodified upstream find_fold_pairs with num_pairs=20, original rounding/fallback/downselection

canonical.order: metric.aggregate_item on native raw units, then official _project_unit_scores and _project_item_scores, then official MeanAggregator
canonical.units: canonical score dimensionless; score_raw spatial pixels, style Gram cosine distance, lighting native lighting distance
canonical.report_percent: multiply canonical score by 100 once for published-table comparison
canonical.trigger: MBench-A drops trigger keys; no judge/API

runtime_adapters: explicit user weights directory with SHA256/size verification; offline snapshot loading
reuse unchanged style bundle and DA3 instances; retain raw-before-project ordering
limits: The official published DA3 producer checkpoint/resize/frame policy is not fully specified. This package reproduces the documented uniform32 producer; exact published-score reproduction is unverified.
Full-frame DA3 and actual processed pixels would define a separate protocol. This package retains the frozen uniform32 sampling and original-pixel policy.
The official mean summary averages available score keys even for an invalid item. Calibration acceptance must require both item.valid and a finite score; canonical receipts remain unchanged.
